recipes.name: Winter Blossom's Often Requested Ham Salad

steps.text: Add ham to the bowl of a food processor; pulse until finely chopped but not pasty, 6 or 7 pulses. (You may need to do this in batches.) Transfer to a large bowl; repeat with remaining ham.
Stir mayonnaise, onion, relish, and mustard into chopped ham mixture until well combined; add more mayonnaise if mixture is too dry. Chill ham salad until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Winter Blossom's Often Requested Ham Salad
raw_recipe.description: This often requested ham salad recipe is easy to make with chopped ham, mayonnaise, pickle relish, and mustard. Serve for parties, lunch, or breakfast.

review.reviewBody: Hi Folks, I want to thank you for your nice reviews. Glad you enjoy the salad as much as my friends and family do. Just wanted to mention, if there is any left over it is great mixed with a little Italian flavored bread crumbs and stuffed in mushrooms then baked for 1/2 hour at 325 for an appetizer. You might even add some grated Parmesan to the top just before removing from the oven. A friend has made this salad with left over roast pork and it is also very tasty. I grind almost everything left over and give it a try. I had two left over Chicken Cordon Blue's the other day, ground them up and made chicken salad and it was awesome. The combination of the cheese and the ham made it delicious. Thanks again for the reviews. Happy days and happy grinding. :o] Winter Blossom

Very good! I did just what the description below the recipe dictated and marched right up to my deli counter and asked for the ham ends, along with enough ham to make 1 1/2 lbs. I did use light mayo and fresh onion, as I didn't have any dry minced onion on hand. I don't know about serving twelve...my three boys asked for second sandwiches and I spread some on Toppers crackers. Aside from a little leftover, it's gone gone gone. I'll make this again!

Oh my, a blast from the past! my mom made this often from leftover ham or for "tea" sandwiches for a luncheon. We had one of those hand grinders that clamped to the table and we'd run the ham, onions & pickles thru it. Mix with mayo & mustard and presto! Also did the same with leftover chuck roast ( actually used a huge roast just to have leftovers). Love this stuff! Sometimes she'd throw hard boiled eggs to grind along with the meat. Since we had our own chickens they were an inexpensive way to stretch the meat.

I have to admit that I had never even tried ham salad prior to making this recipe. I had to serve a large crowd and didn't have enough chicken for chicken salad, but had leftover ham. I stumbled across this recipe and decided to give it a shot. It is surprisingly good! I ended up just chopping up pickles since I didn't have relish. The consistency was fine, but the juice made it a little salty. I would recommend drying them in a paper towel if you go this route. Thanks, Winter Blossom!

This turned out very good. I only had 1 1/4 lb. of left over ham. I made the dressing as directed, and still had to add just a tad more mayo. I minced the ham very fine in my processor. I also always hydrate my dried minced onion before adding to my recipes. Just a preference so it doesn't have to sit for hours to make the onion soft. I personally think this recipe would be perfect by keeping everything just like it is, but only using 1 lb. of ham. Especially if the ham is finely shredded. After making the dressing I was just a little worried since it didn't taste like what i am used to, but after everything went together it turned out so good.

Yummy. Just plain yummy. Use good quality ham. Thanks from one blondie to another! Tip: my mom used to add a heaping tablespoon of orange marmalade to her ham salad if it was a particularly salty ham. It adds another flavor to this already delicious sandwich spread.

This is pretty good. I used leftover "honeybaked"-style ham and some of the sweetness of that is taking over the relish, onion, and mustard flavoring. I will probably try to make this another time using smoked or boiled ham. REVISION: I increased this from 4 to 5 stars because after a couple of days in the frig, this tasted fantastic (even using the honey-baked)!
I'd recommend using a meat grinder with a small cutting plate. I use my grandmother's hand crank grinder. I like the texture better. I've also substituted balogna following her depression era recipe.

My husband loves ham salad but is very fussy. This one met with his approval. I like to use fresh onion, so I finely chopped onion in the food processor and substituted it for the dried onion. I also used sweet pickle relish and added more mayo. This gave the salad the sweet, moist salad that we prefer. I will be making this again.

Perfect. I bought a ham steak just for this recipe. Used what I had on hand: sweet pickles and dijon, along with the dried minced onions and mayo. I will try it with dill relish and fresh onions next time, but this was delish! The proportions of ingredients were just right.
ok but would use Dukes mayonnaise, and chop a real onion for flavor.
I have been making this same ham salad recipe for years - our whole family loves it. The only thing I do different is that I add celery - the crunch factor makes it even better!

I made the recipe as listed using a small 1/2 regular ham without glaze. The dried minced onion ruined it for me. It added a very sweet strange flavor. I don’t like sweet ham salad, which is why I chose a recipe with dill relish as opposed to sweet relish. I tried to rescue it, adding some fresh, diced white onion, and some diced celery, which helped a little but the odd flavor persisted. I will make it again though, but just with regular onion next time.
To add additional flavor, I added two chopped hard-boiled eggs and half an orange bell pepper chopped. I also added black pepper to taste.

There was a little diner when I was a child that served grilled ham salad sandwiches. I have never found a recipe until this one that closely mirrors the flavor of those amazing sandwiches from my childhood. Thank you so much. They are perfect. Just the way the recipe is written
Great use of leftover holiday ham!

This is very close to my recipe that I've been making for years. I use a little more crunchy veg, varies by what I have on hand. Celery, green onions, green peppers, sometimes jalapeno. Also, I hand chop the ham as I like the pieces to be a little bigger than from a grinder.

When I was in college they served the best ham salad. I've searched high and low for a recipe that met that high standard. My search has ended! This recipe is the best! Whenever I have leftover ham I whip up a batch of this ham salad. It takes me back to my days at college. Yum!

I have been making this salad for many years. Sometimes I add a lil marmalade. Back in the day when I had 5 teens at home, I would make it with 3 cans of Treet canned meat or Spam, whichever was cheaper. My 3 boys loved it in sandwiches, my 2 girls on whatever crackers we had in hand. They all make it for their children now!
Loved the taste of the pickle relishin this! I made it just as recipe said. had it with crackers. Fam loved it!
